thread:
Aisha: FYI Sales -> HorizonFlow reported a p95 regression after last night's maintenance. Putting intake here. Ticket: https://support.redwood.example/t/HF-9001
Tom: Theysee p95 ~720ms (SLA 300ms) around 02:05 UTC. QPS ~11. Model: `hf-thera-quant-v1` on Dedicated (eu-west).
Rajat: Release notes show runtime bump runt-2.20 plus a change to default batching policy (continuous batching tweaks). No routing changes. I'll try to repro.
Clara: Customer provided scrubbed sample and token distro: most 150-900 tokens, ~8% >1200. Payload: `{\"prompt\":\"Extract allergy list\",\"max_tokens\":180}`
ops-bot: deploy-bot: PROD deploy runt-2.20 finished 2026-04-10T01:48:02Z
Aisha: Product proposes P1 (SLA breach for paid Dedicated). Closure criteria: 1) mitigation deployed (rollback or config) OR routing workaround; 2) p95 <= 320ms for 1 hour under comparable load; 3) customer updates every 60m until resolved. Agree?
Tom: Quick checks: did we change batching defaults + quantized variant at same time? That combo could increase per-request tail latency under low QPS due to batching timers. Also continuous-batch + KV-cache interplay could be odd.
Rajat: Good point. We did change batching heuristics in runt-2.20: lower max-wait to favor latencyless small batches. But for quantized kernels that fallback to a slower execution path, smaller batches could increase kernel-switch overhead.
Clara: So two hypotheses: 1) batching heuristic interacts poorly with quantized kernel selection causing occasional slow path, 2) KV-cache warmup/preservation change. Both could impact p95 but have different mitigations.
Tom: Mitigations: (A) flip batching policy back to previous ctx for that pool (config flip) ~15-30m to canary; (B) rollback runtime to runt-2.19 ~30-45m canary + validate; (C) route customer to alternate pool temporarily (manual routing) ~10-20m but requires coordination.
Rajat: I'll repro in staging with their token histogram and the new batching settings. Posting flamegraphs and trace spans in ~40m. Need a redacted recent request log for timing spikes if possible.
Clara: Customer wants hourly updates. Sales asked about SLA credits if >24h. Please include that in comms.
ops-bot: rollback-run-2312350200 queued (manual approval required)
Aisha: Product asks Eng for a short runbook: steps to canary config flip, rollback plan, monitoring checks (p50/p95/batch-size-dist/kernel-path-rates/kv-hit), and customer message template. Also need backlog ticket to add CI gating for batching changes vs quantized models.
Tom: I'll start a targeted load with 11 qps and token tail to see if p95 reproduces. Early thought: if batch-size-dist shows many singleton or tiny batches, that supports the batching-timer/overhead theory.
Rajat: Repro started. Early logs: p50 flat, p95 spikes match requests that incurred `kernel_fallback=true` in traces and batch-size 1-2. Posting initial spans to ticket.
Clara: If that confirms batching problem, config flip to previous batching defaults on their pool seems low-risk and fast. That avoids rollback.
Aisha: Good. Product will prioritize immediate config canary first. If config doesn't fix, do rollback. Also record acceptance tests: synthetic test with quantized variant, batching timers, long-seq tail, assert p95 < 320ms for 10 qps for 1 hour.
Rajat: Noted. I'll attach artifacts to PROD ticket REDWOOD-HF-9001 and tag eng-runtime. Will update within 45m.
Tom: Action items: Rajat repro + logs, Tom prepare config-canary steps, Aisha coordinate comms with Sales, Clara collect customer timing logs.
sales: Customer confirmed they received initial ack and appreciate the quick loop. :thumbsup:
Aisha: Closing thread for intake. Continuing in PROD ticket for fixes and comms.
